scheme_name: Promotion of Tiatr Through Academic Activities
description:
The Promotion of Tiatr Through Academic Activities is a government welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Goa.

This scheme was launched in the year 2018.

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote the traditional art form of Tiatr.

Tiatr is a popular form of theatre in Goa that combines drama, music, and dance.

The scheme aims to enhance the cultural heritage of Goa by supporting Tiatr artists and promoting this art form among the youth.

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to conduct workshops and training sessions for aspiring Tiatr artists.

These workshops are designed to improve the skills of participants in acting, scriptwriting, and stage management.

The government has set a goal to conduct at least 10 workshops annually under this scheme.

Each workshop can accommodate up to 50 participants.

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance to Tiatr artists for their productions.

The government provides a grant of up to ₹2 lakh for each Tiatr production.

This financial support is aimed at covering expenses related to staging, costumes, and other production costs.

Additionally, the scheme facilitates the organization of Tiatr festivals.

These festivals serve as a platform for artists to showcase their talents and gain recognition.

The festivals also help in attracting audiences and promoting Tiatr as a cultural activity.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of Goa.

Applicants must also be involved in the Tiatr art form either as performers or as part of the production team.

There are no specific age limits for applicants.

However, preference is given to youth and emerging artists.

The application process for the scheme involves several steps.

Interested individuals or groups must submit an application to the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa.

The application must include details of the proposed Tiatr production and a budget estimate.

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and a detailed project proposal.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by a committee formed by the Directorate of Art and Culture.

The committee evaluates the proposals based on artistic merit and feasibility.

Successful applicants are notified within 30 days of application submission.

Disbursement of funds is made in two installments.

The first installment is released upon approval of the project.

The second installment is released after submission of a utilization certificate and a report on the conducted activities.

The scheme operates on an annual basis with a budget allocation of ₹50 lakh.

This budget is utilized for grants, workshops, and festival organization.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa.

The Directorate is responsible for overseeing the implementation and monitoring of the scheme.

Contact details for the Directorate of Art and Culture are available on the official Goa government website.

The scheme has seen participation from various local Tiatr troupes.

These troupes have benefited from the financial assistance provided under the scheme.

In 2020, a total of 15 Tiatr productions received funding.

This funding helped in reviving interest in Tiatr during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The government also encourages collaboration between Tiatr artists and educational institutions.

This collaboration aims to introduce Tiatr as part of the curriculum in schools and colleges.

The scheme has received positive feedback from the Tiatr community.

Artists have expressed gratitude for the support provided by the government.

The initiative has contributed to the preservation of the Tiatr art form.

It has also helped in creating job opportunities for artists and technicians.

The scheme aligns with the broader cultural policy of the Government of Goa.

This policy emphasizes the importance of preserving and promoting local art forms.

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to promote Tiatr among the youth.

These campaigns aim to attract new audiences and participants to the art form.

The scheme is part of the government's efforts to enhance cultural tourism in Goa.

By promoting Tiatr, the government hopes to attract more tourists interested in local culture.

The scheme has been instrumental in fostering a sense of community among Tiatr artists.

It has provided a platform for collaboration and networking among artists.

The government plans to expand the scope of the scheme in the coming years.

Future plans include increasing the budget allocation to ₹1 crore by 2025.

This increase will allow for more extensive workshops and larger festivals.

The government also aims to introduce online platforms for Tiatr performances.

These platforms will help artists reach a wider audience beyond Goa.

The Promotion of Tiatr Through Academic Activities is a significant step towards cultural preservation.

It highlights the importance of supporting traditional art forms in modern society.

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the arts and culture sector.

It reflects an understanding of the role of culture in community identity and cohesion.

Overall, the scheme has made a positive impact on the Tiatr community in Goa.

It continues to inspire new generations of artists to engage with this vibrant art form.
